title: Around Circular Quay
intro: Five places within a few minutes' walk of the ferries. A gentle start.

steps.riddle: Start with the city's signature: the performing arts centre whose roofs are a cluster of white shells.
hints: It occupies the whole of the point between Sydney Cove and Farm Cove.
steps.reveal: The Sydney Opera House, by the Danish architect Jørn Utzon, formally opened by Queen Elizabeth II on 20 October 1973. It covers the whole of Bennelong Point.

steps.ask: They call it the Coathanger. In what year did the Harbour Bridge open?
steps.reveal: 1932. Built by Dorman Long of Middlesbrough under the direction of John Bradfield, the bridge was formally opened on Saturday, 19 March 1932.

steps.riddle: Find the small sandstone house built in 1816 for the government's coxswains, once almost at the water's edge.
hints: It is at 110 George Street, The Rocks.
steps.reveal: Cadmans Cottage. At high tide the water came within 2.4 metres of it; since the land was reclaimed for Circular Quay, the shore is about 100 metres away.

steps.ask: The Museum of Contemporary Art on Circular Quay moved into a building put up for whom?
options: The Bank of New South Wales
steps.reveal: The Maritime Services Board. The museum, established in 1991, is housed in the board's former Stripped Classical and Art Deco building on the western side of Circular Quay.

steps.ask: Customs House stands at the head of Circular Quay. When was it built?
steps.reveal: 1845, to designs by Mortimer Lewis. It housed the customs until 1988 and is now home to the City of Sydney Library.

title: Shops and stages
intro: The arcades, picture palaces and department stores of the city centre.

steps.riddle: Find the Romanesque Revival marketplace that fills a whole city block.
hints: The block is bounded by George, Market, York and Druitt streets.
steps.reveal: The Queen Victoria Building, designed by George McRae and built between 1893 and 1898: 30 metres wide and 190 metres long.

steps.ask: The Strand Arcade runs from Pitt Street Mall to George Street. When did it open?
steps.reveal: 1892, after two years of building. It is the only remaining arcade of its kind in Sydney.

steps.riddle: Find the picture palace on Market Street that has been home to the Sydney Film Festival since 1974.
steps.reveal: The State Theatre, designed by Henry Eli White with John Eberson and built between 1926 and 1929.

steps.ask: The Downing Centre on Liverpool Street houses courts today. What was it built as?
steps.reveal: A department store: Mark Foy's Piazza Store, built for Mark Foy in 1908 to designs by Arthur Anderson and much extended in 1927–1930.

steps.riddle: Finally, look up: find the tower that stands 309 metres above the city, the tallest structure in Sydney.
hints: It rises from a shopping centre between Pitt, Market and Castlereagh streets.
steps.reveal: Sydney Tower, long known as Centrepoint Tower. It sits above the Westfield Sydney shopping centre.

title: Macquarie Street and the park
intro: Convicts, rum and the oldest public buildings of the colony, along the street Governor Macquarie built.

steps.riddle: Find the brick barracks a convict architect designed to house convict men and boys.
steps.reveal: Hyde Park Barracks, built between 1817 and 1819 to designs by the convict architect Francis Greenway. It is one of the eleven Australian Convict Sites on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

steps.ask: The Sydney Mint was built between 1811 and 1816 as one wing of a hospital. What was the hospital called?
steps.reveal: The Rum Hospital: its builders were paid with 45,000 gallons of rum. The Mint, its southern wing, is the oldest surviving public building in the city centre.

steps.ask: The Great Synagogue faces Hyde Park from Elizabeth Street. When was it finished?
steps.reveal: 1878, after four years' building to designs by Thomas Rowe. Its congregation is the oldest in Sydney's Jewish community.

steps.riddle: Find the Art Deco war memorial in the southern half of Hyde Park.
steps.reveal: The Anzac Memorial, designed by C. Bruce Dellit with sculpture by Rayner Hoff, built from 1932 to 1934 and opened on 24 November 1934.

steps.ask: St Andrew's Cathedral stands beside the Town Hall. What does it claim?
steps.reveal: The oldest cathedral in Australia: designed mainly by Edmund Blacket, built from 1837 and consecrated in 1868.

title: Pubs of The Rocks
intro: Which is Sydney's oldest pub? Walk the ridge above the harbour and judge for yourself.

steps.ask: The Lord Nelson in Millers Point is the oldest working licensed hotel in Sydney. When was it built?
steps.reveal: Around 1814 to 1815, by the Irish-born stonemason James Dempsey.

steps.riddle: Find the pub on Lower Fort Street, Millers Point, built from 1843 to 1844.
hints: Its name remembers Wellington's great battle.
steps.reveal: The Hero of Waterloo Hotel, built from 1843 to 1844.

steps.ask: The Fortune of War on George Street advertises itself as Sydney's oldest pub. Why is that contested?
options: Its present building only dates from 1922
It lost its licence for twenty years
steps.reveal: The pub was first built in 1828, but the present building dates from 1922, so the Lord Nelson and the Hero of Waterloo contest the title.

steps.riddle: Find the row of workers' cottages and a corner store on Gloucester Street, lived in until 1990 and now a museum.
steps.reveal: Susannah Place: a grocery store and workers' cottages, built during 1844, with domestic occupants until 1990.

steps.riddle: End at church: find the first military church built in colonial Australia.
steps.reveal: The Garrison Church, Holy Trinity, built from 1840 to 1846; Edmund Blacket designed its second stage.

title: Up and across the harbour
intro: The towers that broke Sydney's skyline, and the houses across the water. With the colours off, mostly.

steps.ask: The AWA Tower on York Street is a radio mast on an office building. When was it finished?
steps.reveal: 1939. It was Australia's tallest building until the 115-metre AMP Building was built in 1962.

steps.riddle: Find the skyscraper that was the tallest building in Sydney from 1992 to 2019.
steps.reveal: Chifley Tower, 53 storeys, designed by Kohn Pedersen Fox with Travis McEwen.

steps.riddle: Now find the tower that overtook it in 2020, built on the paved-over wharves of Barangaroo.
hints: It is 271 metres tall, with 75 floors.
steps.reveal: Crown Sydney, also known as One Barangaroo: 271.3 metres, the tallest building in Sydney.

steps.riddle: Cross the harbour: find the 83-metre apartment block at McMahons Point that some critics call one of Sydney's ugliest buildings.
steps.reveal: Blues Point Tower, 83 metres tall with 144 apartments over 24 levels.

steps.ask: Two official residences share Kirribilli Point. Admiralty House is the Governor-General's; whose is Kirribilli House?
options: The Premier of New South Wales's
steps.reveal: The Prime Minister's: Kirribilli House is the secondary official residence of the prime minister, beside Admiralty House, the governor-general's Sydney residence.
